name: Travelers Insurance

profile.address: South 150th Street, Papillion, Sarpy County, Nebraska, 68059
profile.reading:
This data center in Sarpy County, Nebraska, in the La Vista and Papillion area south of Omaha, is a private enterprise facility built and operated by Travelers Insurance, the primary operating subsidiary of The Travelers Companies, a Hartford, Connecticut headquartered property and casualty insurer that traces its roots back to the 19th century and today ranks among the largest insurers in the United States.

Before Travelers publicly confirmed it was the company behind the project, the development moved through local approvals under the code name Project Oasis, a practice large corporations commonly use for major facility construction so that land acquisition and public incentive negotiations are not complicated by a well known corporate name driving up prices or public expectations ahead of time. Once the identity became public, local and national trade coverage, including reporting from Data Center Dynamics, the Omaha World Herald, and Insurance Journal, described the project as a roughly 200 million dollar investment and placed its opening around 2015, part of a broader wave of large scale data center construction that Sarpy County attracted through the 2010s as companies sought sites with available power, favorable tax treatment, and proximity to Omaha's existing fiber and workforce base.

Unlike a colocation or wholesale facility, the Travelers site is not marketed to outside tenants. It exists to run the company's own internal systems, which for a major property and casualty insurer means policy administration platforms, claims processing systems that must remain available around the clock, actuarial and underwriting data, and disaster recovery infrastructure that lets the company keep operating if another facility goes offline, a particularly important consideration for an insurer whose claims volumes can spike sharply after major weather events. Travelers has not published a critical IT load figure in megawatts, total square footage, or a tier certification for the building, which is consistent with how most enterprise owned, single tenant data centers are documented publicly. The parent company discloses what it needs to for local permitting and economic development purposes, in this case largely the investment figure, but treats the technical specifications of a facility supporting its own claims and policy systems as internal operational detail rather than something a competitor or the public needs to see.
